newsitem.title: FRANCE: French magistrates rap government over police.
newsitem.headline: French magistrates rap government over police.

text.p: Two top magistrates criticised France's government for backing Paris' crime squad chief after a court suspended him for refusing to help a corruption probe into the ruling Gaullist party, the justice ministry said on Tuesday.

A Paris court last month ordered Olivier Foll suspended from for six months after he told police not to help a magistrate search the home of Paris Mayor Jean Tiberi in July in a probe into funding of the Gaullist Rally for the Republic (RPR).
Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre, who is close to President Jacques Chirac, said the court had "gone too far" in ordering Foll suspended. Debre had also publicly supported Foll's original decision.

A justice ministry spokesman confirmed reports that Pierre Truche, president of the Cour de Cassation, France's supreme court, complained in a letter to Justice Minister Jacques Toubon about Debre's support of Foll.
"I regret that a member of the government has cast doubt on magistrates who acted within their duty," read an excerpt of Truche's letter published in the daily newspaper Le Monde.
The spokesman also confirmed that Guy Canivet, president of the Paris appeals court, wrote to Debre to express his concern that the minister had questioned a judicial decision.
Magistrates' unions had criticised Toubon for not condemning Debre's support of Foll, while the opposition Socialists accused the government of trying to interfere with justice.
"Mr Toubon's position is that judicial decisions must be respected, as well as the men who take them," the ministry spokesman said.
Both letters were sent on October 30.
Magistrate Eric Halphen went ahead and carried out the search on his own in an investigation focusing on allegations of kickbacks to the RPR in connection with Paris housing contracts.
Foll, who is appealing the suspension, has complained that Halphen only told the policemen when they got to Tiberi's door whose home they were going to search.
